title: brachyglottis stewartiae
intro: Brachyglottis stewartiae, commonly known as Kawakawa, is a plant species native to New Zealand. Kawakawa is a small, evergreen tree in the family Compositae, with a long history of traditional use in Maori medicine. The plant is valued for its potential health benefits, which include anti-inflammatory and antioxidant properties, and is used to treat various conditions such as arthritis, wounds, and digestive issues. The bioactive constituents of Kawakawa include alkaloids, flavonoids, and sesquiterpenes, which are responsible for its therapeutic actions of reducing pain, inflammation, and promoting wound healing.
